title: 7-round AES-256: Basic differential: full-key claim

target.description: Reduced 7-round AES-256 with whitening k_-1, final MixColumns omitted, and u_i=MC^-1(k_i). Four whitening bytes, four u6 bytes and one u5 byte (72 bits of named round-key material). Step2c proposes exhaustive search of the remaining key; the online headline does not separately budget that completion for this instance.

setting.key_relation: One fixed standard AES schedule; no related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: General fixed key; no weak-key subset is specified.
setting.plaintext_model: 2^81 diagonal structures of2^32 blocks; expected right pair under2^-120 differential.
assumptions: The four-round one-byte differential is modeled at2^-120; Observation5 enumerates middle states using an average S-box count.
Wrong-key multisets are modeled random. The journal's separate probability proof has documented count/max-probability issues.
Reported time is the online stage; preprocessing is explicit and key-independent. Partial-encryption conversion factors are author estimates.

success.description: No numerical finite-budget success is supplied for this exact key_recovery endpoint. Expected right-pair counts, table coverage and wrong-key rejection are distinct from complete-output success. The existing Observation5 average-to-uniform enumeration conflict remains. Section5.1 uses2^81 structures of2^32 plaintexts, with source expected filters leaving2^48, then2^24, then one pair per key hypothesis. The remaining-key search and optional repetition do not have a numerical joint success. The2^-136 bound printed by DTCB09 is not a DKS multiset bound. The full-key author headline does not supply a separately quantified completion probability.
